text: In reported speech, which of the following is the correct form of the modal verb 'can'?
options: I can speak English fluently.
I could speak English fluently.
I was able to speak English fluently.
I am able to speak English fluently.
explanation: In reported speech, the modal verb 'can' changes to 'could' to indicate a past ability or possibility. This is because the original statement was in the present tense, but in reported speech, we use the past tense to indicate that the ability or possibility has passed.
subject: English

text: Which of the following sentences is an example of a third conditional sentence?
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I pass the exam, I will be happy.
I would have passed the exam if I had studied harder.
I will pass the exam if I study harder.
correctAnswer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
explanation: A third conditional sentence is used to talk about a past situation that did not happen and its hypothetical consequences. It is formed using the past perfect tense in the if-clause and the conditional tense in the main clause.
subject: English

text: Identify the parallel structure in the following sentence: 'I love reading books, writing stories and to travel.'
options: I love reading books, writing stories and to travel.
I love reading books, writing stories and traveling.
I love reading books, to write stories and travel.
I love reading books, writing stories and going on trips.
correctAnswer: I love reading books, writing stories and traveling.
explanation: Parallel structure is used to maintain consistency in the grammatical form of words or phrases in a sentence. In this case, the three items in the list should be in the same grammatical form, so 'traveling' is the correct choice.
subject: English

text: Which of the following sentences is an example of subject-verb inversion?
options: The sun rises in the east.
The sun sets in the west.
The teacher gave the student a book.
The student was given a book by the teacher.
correctAnswer: The student was given a book by the teacher.
explanation: Subject-verb inversion is a grammatical construction in which the order of the subject and verb is reversed. In this case, the subject 'the student' is followed by the verb 'was given' in the passive voice, which is an example of subject-verb inversion.
subject: English

text: Identify the grammatical discrepancy in the following sentence: 'The manager of the company, who is very experienced, have been working here for 10 years.'
options: The manager of the company, who is very experienced, have been working here for 10 years.
The manager of the company, who is very experienced, has been working here for 10 years.
The manager of the company, who is very experienced, was working here for 10 years.
The manager of the company, who is very experienced, is working here for 10 years.
correctAnswer: The manager of the company, who is very experienced, has been working here for 10 years.
explanation: The grammatical discrepancy in this sentence is the subject-verb agreement error. The subject 'the manager' is singular, so the verb 'has been working' should be used instead of 'have been working'.

text: Which of the following sentences is an example of a zero conditional sentence?
options: Water freezes at 0°C.
If I don't study, I will fail the exam.
I will pass the exam if I study hard.
The sun rises in the east.
explanation: A zero conditional sentence is used to talk about universal truths or facts. It is formed using the simple present tense in both the if-clause and the main clause.
subject: English

text: Identify the correct form of the conditional sentence: 'If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.'
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I study harder, I will pass the exam.
If I had studied harder, I will pass the exam.
If I study harder, I would have passed the exam.
correctAnswer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
explanation: The correct form of the conditional sentence is the third conditional, which is used to talk about a past situation that did not happen and its hypothetical consequences. It is formed using the past perfect tense in the if-clause and the conditional tense in the main clause.

text: Which of the following sentences is an example of a first conditional sentence?
options: If I don't study, I will fail the exam.
I will pass the exam if I study hard.
Water freezes at 0°C.
The sun rises in the east.
correctAnswer: I will pass the exam if I study hard.
explanation: A first conditional sentence is used to talk about a future situation that is likely to happen. It is formed using the present simple tense in the if-clause and the future simple tense in the main clause.

text: Identify the correct form of the sentence: 'The manager of the company, who is very experienced, have been working here for 10 years.'
options: The manager of the company, who is very experienced, have been working here for 10 years.
The manager of the company, who is very experienced, has been working here for 10 years.

The manager of the company, who is very experienced, is working here for 10 years.
correctAnswer: The manager of the company, who is very experienced, has been working here for 10 years.
explanation: The correct form of the sentence is the present perfect tense, which is used to talk about an action that started in the past and continues up to the present. In this case, the manager has been working here for 10 years.
